{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOBGLqvc8AAAABVDv38A", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BlvlNzg-kavw", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BlvlN", "number": 5, "title": "Migrate mmd-parser source to strict TypeScript with minimal type escapes", "body": "## Problem

The source is currently JavaScript and constructs many parser result objects incrementally (for example `var p = {}; p.position = ...`). This makes the PMD/PMX/VMD/VPD data shapes implicit and leaves important format constraints—tuple lengths, index sizes, discriminated record types, optional sections, and coordinate-system state—unchecked.

We want to migrate the project to TypeScript without turning the type system into documentation-only. In particular, the migration should avoid broad escape hatches such as `any`, `@ts-ignore`, `@ts-nocheck`, or pervasive type assertions that bypass compiler checks.

## Expected outcome

The maintained source is TypeScript, with explicit, reusable types for the public parser results and internal binary-reading structures. The project builds and exposes the same public API and runtime behavior as today, while TypeScript catches invalid or incomplete parser data structures.

The migration should aim for zero explicit `any` in project-owned code. Where an external package lacks types, add a narrow local declaration or typed adapter instead of propagating `any`. Type assertions should be rare, locally justified, and not used to paper over incomplete object construction.

## Scope

- Convert the maintained source entry point and modules to TypeScript:
  - `index.js`
  - `src/Parser.js`
  - `src/DataViewEx.js`
  - `src/DataCreationHelper.js`
  - `src/CharsetEncoder.js`
- Define explicit types for PMD, PMX, VMD, and VPD parser outputs, including metadata and nested records.
- Use tuple types or equivalent fixed-shape helpers for values such as Vector2, Vector3, quaternions, skin indices/weights, and other fixed-length binary fields where practical.
- Model PMX variants (for example deform/skinning and morph element types) with discriminated unions or similarly type-safe structures instead of broad mutable objects.
- Type binary index sizes as the supported finite set (1, 2, or 4 bytes) and keep signed/unsigned handling explicit.
- Configure TypeScript with `strict: true` and enable checks that prevent implicit `any`; enable `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` unless a specific repository-owned pattern cannot reasonably satisfy it without reducing clarity.
- Add a typed boundary for `charset-encoder-js` if its published typings are insufficient.
- Update the build configuration and development dependencies only as needed to compile/bundle the TypeScript source and continue producing the existing distributable outputs used by `package.json`.
- Preserve the existing public exports and usage patterns, including `MMDParser`, `Parser`, `CharsetEncoder`, browser usage through the built bundle, and the current parser method names/signatures at runtime.
- Update repository documentation where source/build instructions or file names change.

Out of scope:

- Implementing currently unsupported PMX features or changing parser semantics as part of the migration.
- Unrelated dependency modernization, CI/deployment work, formatting rewrites, or API redesign.
- Version/release publication unless handled by a separate release task.

## Reproduction (when relevant)

Not applicable. This is a maintainability and type-safety migration rather than a runtime bug report.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] Project-owned TypeScript source compiles under `strict: true` with no explicit `any`, `@ts-ignore`, or `@ts-nocheck`.
- [ ] Any necessary type assertions are narrowly scoped, justified by a runtime-checked boundary or external API, and are not used to construct partially typed parser result objects.
- [ ] PMD, PMX, VMD, and VPD parser result structures have exported or otherwise reusable explicit types, with discriminated unions/fixed-length tuples used where they materially improve correctness.
- [ ] `DataViewEx` and related binary helpers expose type-safe APIs for fixed-length values and supported index sizes without requiring callers to cast ordinary parser data.
- [ ] Insufficient third-party typings are handled through a narrow declaration/adapter rather than leaking `any` into parser code.
- [ ] The existing public runtime API and export names remain compatible unless a specific unavoidable incompatibility is documented in the PR.
- [ ] The applicable build completes and produces the distributable bundle files expected by `package.json`.
- [ ] A TypeScript type-check command is documented and passes; applicable parser tests/smoke checks are run after rebuilding. Because the current test script depends on external `cdn.rawgit.com` samples, download failures or unexercised PMX behavior are reported accurately and are not described as passing coverage.
- [ ] Generated bundle changes are reviewed, and unrelated dependency upgrades or parser feature changes are not included.
- [ ] `Readme.md` and development guidance remain accurate for installation, build, test, and source-file paths after the migration.

## Required post-merge verification

None.
